a:r.a:t: Activator-binding sites are near promoters that weakly bind RNA Pol or do not bind at all.
It may remain bound until a molecule signals dissociation.
Alternatively, the activator may only bind when signaled.

p:cNvPr.descr: Part C: A four-part diagram illustrating the common patterns of regulation of transcription initiation; parts a and b show negative regulation, and parts c and d show positive regulation. In part a, a mid-sized, narrow rectangular structure is divided into three segments by black lines. Starting from the left, the first segment is short and blue, and labeled DNA. The next segment is longer and purple, and labeled, Promoter. Towards the right end of this segment, an orange egg-like structure is shown with a crack at the top, creating a V; this is labeled Repressor. To the right of the purple segment is a yellow segment that is slightly shorter. Above the line that separates the purple and yellow segments is a short arrow that points up, and then right to bold red letters that say, "OFF." Below this structure is an arrow pointing down. To its left, a small green diamond shape, labeled Molecular signal, enters the process; this is illustrated by a small arrow that curves into the arrow pointing down. The two arrows point to another mid-sized, narrow rectangular structure, this time, divided into five segments: a short blue one on the left, followed by a longer light purple one, followed by a significantly shorter, darker purple segment, a tiny light purple, and the yellow at the end. The darker purple segment is labeled, Operator, and above the line that separates the tiny light purple and yellow segments is a short arrow that points up, and then right to bold green letters that say, "ON." Below the yellow segment, a short arrow points down to a wavy green line, labeled mRNA. To the left of that is the orange egg-like structure described earlier; however, this time, the V-shaped crack on top is filled with the green molecular signal. Text above this entire schematic reads, “Negative regulation – Molecular signal causes dissociation of repressor from DNA, inducing transcription.” To the right of this is part b, which starts out with the same structure described in the second half of part a, except this time, the orange egg with the molecular signal is no longer below. Instead, there’s an arrow pointing down, and to the left, a red molecular signal curves into the arrow; to the right, the repressor described at the beginning is shown entering the process. Below the arrow pointing down is the same structure described at the beginning of image a, but this time, the red molecular signal is lodged at the top of the orange structure where the crack is located. The entire schematic reads, “Negative regulation – Molecular signal causes binding of repressor to DNA, inhibiting transcription.” In part c, the same narrow rectangular structure is shown, but this time, it is divided into four segments. Starting from the left is a short, light blue segment, followed by a dark blue segment of the same length, labeled as the activator binding site, followed by a longer purple segment, followed by a yellow segment the length of the blue segments. Above the dark blue segment is a light green ovular structure with an indentation at the top; this is labeled as the activator. To the right of the activator, a purple globular mass, labeled as RNA polymerase, rests on top of the purple segment. Above the line that separates the purple and yellow segments is a short arrow that points up, and then right to bold green letters that say, "ON." Below the yellow segment is a short arrow pointing down to a green wavy line, labeled as mRNA. Below this structure is an arrow pointing down. To its left, another arrow curves into it, indicating the introduction of the red, diamond-shaped molecular signal into the process. Below the two arrows is the same rectangular structure just described, but this time, the activator is below the rectangular line, and the red molecular signal is bound to the top of the activator. Also, the arrow that separates the purple and yellow segments points right to bold red letters that say, "OFF." This schematic reads, “Positive regulation – Molecular signal causes dissociation of activator from DNA, inhibiting transcription.” In part d, the same structure described at the end of part c is shown. Below it is an arrow that points down. To its left, a green, diamond-shaped molecular signal is shown entering the process by way of a short arrow that curves into the arrow pointing down. To its right, the light-green activator is shown entering the process by way of an arrow curving into the arrow pointing down. Below these arrows is a similar structure as the one described at the beginning of part c, but this time, the green molecular signal is lodged into the crack at the top of the activator, which sits on top of the dark blue segment. Everything else is the same as the first structure in part c. This entire schematic reads, “Positive regulation – Molecular signal causes binding of activator to DNA, inducing transcription.”
